sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

By the end of this lesson you'll understand how Zapier works, how it compares to n8n, and how to build an automation that uses an AI step to process data between two apps.

## What is Zapier?

Zapier is the most widely used no-code automation platform. It connects 6,000+ apps and requires zero technical setup — you work entirely in a browser interface with no canvas to arrange, just a step-by-step form.

The core concept:
- A **Zap** = one automation (trigger + one or more actions)
- **Trigger**: something that happens in App A
- **Action**: something that happens in App B (and C, and D...)
- **AI by Zapier**: a special action that runs a prompt on your data in the middle of a Zap

Zapier is built around ease of use. If you've never automated anything before, Zapier is the fastest path from idea to running workflow.

**Pricing note:** The "AI by Zapier" action that processes data with an LLM requires a Zapier **paid plan** (Starter, $19.99/month or higher). The free tier does not include AI steps.

If you don't want to pay, you already built three real AI automations in lesson 10-2 using n8n Cloud's free tier — that's the better free option. This lesson teaches the Zapier concept, which is useful to understand even if you use n8n in practice.

## How Zapier Compares to n8n

| Feature | Zapier | n8n |
|---------|--------|-----|
| Setup | Zero install, browser only | Browser (cloud) or self-host |
| App integrations | 6,000+ | 400+ |
| AI step | AI by Zapier (paid) | Native AI Agent node (free) |
| Free tier | Limited zaps, no AI | Generous free tier, AI included |
| Flexibility | Lower | Higher |
| Best for | Quick setup, mainstream apps | Free, powerful, code-optional |

The choice is usually: **Zapier if you want the most app integrations and don't mind paying; n8n if you want free and more control.**

Many teams use both — Zapier for simple app-to-app connections, n8n for anything with AI processing or custom logic.

## The AI by Zapier Action

When AI by Zapier is added as a step in a Zap, it:
1. Takes text from the previous step (email body, form response, spreadsheet cell, etc.)
2. Runs a prompt you write on that text
3. Returns the processed result as data you can use in the next step

Example prompt: `Extract the action item from this email: {{email_body}}. Return only the action item as one sentence.`

The output — a cleaned-up, processed string — becomes the input for the next action (add to task list, send to Notion, post to Slack, etc.).

This is exactly the trigger → AI processes → action pattern from lesson 10-1, just implemented in Zapier's interface.

sections.title: Email-to-Task Automation
sections.content:
This workshop builds a Zap that watches for emails tagged "Action Required" in Gmail, extracts the task using AI, and creates a task in Google Tasks.

**Setup:**
1. Go to zapier.com and sign up or log in
2. If you have a paid plan, follow all steps. If on the free tier, follow steps 1-5 to understand the flow, then skip the AI step and connect trigger directly to action — you'll still get the non-AI version working.

**Build the Zap:**

**Step 1 — Trigger: Gmail — New Email Matching Search**
1. Click **Create Zap**
2. Search for **Gmail** as your trigger app
3. Choose trigger event: **New Email Matching Search**
4. Connect your Gmail account (OAuth — Zapier never sees your password)
5. Search string: `label:Action-Required` (matches emails you've labeled "Action Required" in Gmail)
6. Test the trigger — Zapier will pull a recent matching email

**Step 2 — Action: AI by Zapier** *(paid plan required)*
1. Add action app: **AI by Zapier**
2. Action event: **Understand & Transform Text**
3. Instructions: `Read the email below and extract only the single most important action item I need to complete. Write it as one clear sentence starting with a verb. Email: {{body_plain}}`
4. Test the action — you'll see the extracted task in the output

**Step 3 — Action: Google Tasks — Create Task**
1. Add action app: **Google Tasks**
2. Action event: **Create Task**
3. Connect your Google account
4. Task title: map to the AI output from Step 2
5. Notes: `From email: {{subject}} — {{sender_name}}`
6. Test the action

**Activate the Zap:**
1. Click **Publish** to turn the Zap on
2. In Gmail, label any email "Action Required"
3. Within ~2 minutes, check Google Tasks — the extracted action item should appear

**What to observe:** The AI step transforms unstructured email text into a clean, actionable task title. Without the AI step you'd have to write a complex filter or accept messy task titles. The AI makes the automation intelligent.

**Zapier's real strength** is breadth of integrations. If you need to connect an obscure CRM to Slack, Zapier almost certainly has both apps. n8n might not. The AI step being paywalled is a real limitation — but for pure app-to-app connections on the free tier, Zapier remains the easiest option.
**You've completed lesson 10-3.** You understand Zapier's model, how AI fits as a processing step, and when to choose Zapier vs n8n. Next: Make's visual approach to the same problem.
